title: The State of Independent Moving Company Websites 2026
note: Aggregates computed from automated scans. No individual site is identified.
attribution: Free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0. Credit Clikiti with a link.
citation: Clikiti. (2026, October 15). The state of independent moving company websites 2026 (Q4 2026) [Report]. https://clikiti.com/research/moving/2026-q4
audience: Web agencies and freelancers selling to independent local, long-distance, storage and specialty moving companies
findings: Only 19% of the 185 independent moving company websites we scanned say whether their estimate is binding, non-binding or not-to-exceed.
A typical site answers four of the nine questions customers planning a move ask before choosing (mean 4.1).
The median overall score is 76 out of 100 (mean 77).
The least-answered questions are "Is the price fixed?" (19%), "What's the deposit, and can I cancel?" (24%) and "What if something breaks?" (31%).
The best-answered are "Will you pack for me?" (85%) and "Can I get a quote without calling?" (84%).

By kind of business, the highest median score is 79 (local residential movers), against 78 for specialty movers: piano, senior and office, 76 for moving and storage companies and 75 for long-distance and interstate movers.
87% fail "Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone" (Core Web Vitals · LCP).
36% fail "MovingCompany or local business structured data" (Schema.org · MovingCompany).

segments.name: Specialty movers: piano, senior and office

agencyProblems.label: Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone
agencyProblems.fix: Resize and compress the hero image, defer chat and tracking scripts, aim for under 2.5 s on a phone.
agencyProblems.pitch: Your home page takes several seconds to appear on a customer's phone.

agencyProblems.label: Text contrast passes 4.5:1
agencyProblems.fix: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 in the theme, especially white text over truck and crew photos.
agencyProblems.pitch: Parts of the site are hard to read, and it is a WCAG failure.

agencyProblems.label: Estimate type named: binding, non-binding or not-to-exceed
agencyProblems.question: Is the price fixed?
agencyProblems.fix: One paragraph, linked from the quote form, that says which kind of estimate the company gives (binding, non-binding or not-to-exceed) and what can change the price on the day.
agencyProblems.pitch: "Is the price fixed?" is the question behind every bad mover story, and your site never answers it.

agencyProblems.label: Deposit or cancellation terms stated
agencyProblems.question: What's the deposit, and can I cancel?
agencyProblems.fix: State the deposit (amount or "no deposit") and the cancellation and rescheduling terms, near the quote form and in the FAQ.
agencyProblems.pitch: A customer about to commit wants to know what they lose if the closing date moves, and your site does not say.

agencyProblems.label: Valuation or moving insurance explained
agencyProblems.question: What if something breaks?
agencyProblems.fix: A short page on what happens if something breaks: released value (60 cents per pound per article) versus full value protection, what each costs and how to claim.
agencyProblems.pitch: Customers find out what basic coverage pays only after something breaks; the movers who explain it first get fewer one-star reviews.
